topStory.headline: Nevada Lawmakers Hear A.I. Education Policy Recommendations
topStory.summary:
Nevada's interim education committee heard testimony on A.I. policy in schools, with recommendations for A.I. training requirements, stronger data privacy protections, and policies ensuring technology aids rather than replaces human interaction, according to the Nevada Current. A committee member noted the recommendations were "geared toward 'we are all for sure going to use this'" rather than examining whether A.I. should be used at all.

A majority of states have issued some form of A.I. guidance for schools. Democratic Assemblymember Selena La Rue Hatch, who is also a teacher, raised concerns about cognitive decline from student over-reliance on A.I. and questioned whether teachers should have the option to refuse using tools they find ethically problematic.

The Guinn Center's research, cited in the hearing, found Nevada educators are already using chatbots for administrative work, lesson planning, and tutoring. The researchers noted there is no reliable long-term data on effectiveness or unintended consequences. The discussion focused on practical guardrails including requiring vendors to meet privacy standards, collecting better data on classroom A.I. use, and prioritizing investments in under-resourced schools.

stories.headline: Cornell Student Alleges A.I. Research Integrity Problems
stories.summary: A Cornell Daily Sun guest column accuses a postdoctoral researcher of publishing shifting, unaccountable principles for A.I. use in academic work without providing evidence for claims about ChatGPT's limitations, according to The Cornell Daily Sun. The piece highlights concerns about research quality in A.I.-related scholarship.

stories.headline: Adobe and Pearson Launch First Firefly A.I. Certification
stories.summary: Adobe and Pearson introduced professional certification for Adobe Firefly, covering prompt engineering and ethical A.I. use in creative workflows, according to Trend Hunter. Adobe research shows 86% of creators now use generative tools daily.

stories.headline: Federal Appeals Court Fines Lawyers $30K for Faulty A.I. Filings
stories.summary: The Sixth Circuit sanctioned two attorneys after finding fake citations and factual errors in appellate briefs, according to Freedom For All Americans. The ruling marks one of the strongest judicial warnings about unreliable A.I.-assisted legal work and signals courts are moving toward tougher penalties for unverified A.I. output.

stories.headline: Penn Students Critique University's A.I. Integration Push
stories.summary: The Daily Pennsylvanian editorial board argues Penn's heavy investment in A.I. programs and research — including the first Ivy League A.I. major — threatens critical thinking development, according to The Daily Pennsylvanian. They cite surveys showing 83% of undergraduates use A.I. academically despite unclear institutional policies.
